text.p: Bulgaria's government on Friday approved the 1997 consolidated state budget draft as part of preparations to launch a currency board system on July 1, Finance Minister Muravei Radev said.
"The cabinet approved this year's budget and will submit it to (committees in) parliament on Monday for approval by the end of the month," Radev told reporters.
A deficit of 5.81 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) was assumed in the central government budget.
A deficit of 6.16 percent was projected in the broader consolidated state budget, which also includes the budgets of the judicial system, the ministries and municipalities.
GDP was assumed at 16,150 billion levs, down a real 7.4 percent from 1996, said Radev. GDP fell a real 10.9 percent last year to 1,660.2 billion levs.

The consolidated budget deficit of 6.16 percent was higher than the IMF-recommended 3.8 percent due to pending interest payments on Bulgarian foreign and domestic debt, but lower than last year's 13 percent.

An exchange rate of 1,000 levs per mark was assumed in the budget as Bulgaria is to introduce on July 1 an IMF-prescribed restrictive fixed exchange rate mechanism, called a currency board, to stabilise the economy.
Annual inflation was seen at 566 percent at end-1997 with average monthly inflation expected at 1.5-2.0 percent in the second half and around one percent by year's end.
Monthly consumer inflation for May was 5.6 percent, bringing cumulative inflation for the first five months to 479.4 percent. Annual inflation last year was 310.8 percent.
Radev said that a trade surplus of over 200 billion levs was assumed in the budget bill as exports were expected to rise in the second half of 1997.
A current account surplus was also assumed in the budget draft and a capital account surplus of $590 million was expected, said Radev.
He added that a totally non-inflationary deficit financing was provided for in the draft through proceeds from privatisation, improved tax collection, domestic debt restructuring and foreign funding.

Central bank lending to the government and commercial banks will be banned under the currency board system and levs in circulation must be fully covered by foreign exchange reserves at a fixed rate of 1,000 levs per mark.
State subsidies will be reduced but will remain in force this year for socially-sensitive sectors like railway and city transport and central heating, Radev said.
Social security payments were assumed at 1.577 trillion levs, defence was allotted 390 billion levs, interior ministry 222 billion levs and state health service 469 billion levs.
Salary payments in the state sector were assumed at 600 billion levs of which some 200 billion levs were distributed in the first half of 1997.
